utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, you're, again, a career police professional. It is the job of the police to arrest suspected perpetrators, particularly of extremely serious crimes, even if that might involve some bloodshed, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was a serious crime, so perhaps it should have been done by a special police unit coming from outside the territory of the Prijedor police station. However, those who were involved in the decision-making about this issue took the decision that they did. I don't know why. I don't think it would be appropriate for me to give my opinion now. Perhaps if I had been in the shoes of the person deciding about it, I would have taken a different position. But I was not competent -- called upon to make this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony you talked about reaching a compromise and the compromise was that this unit would be sent to the front instead of arrested. And then you said: "And if they came back, they would be prosecuted." And that was at page 51. But, in fact, the members of this platoon who came back from the Han Pijesak front were never arrested or prosecuted by the RS authorities, were they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, they were not. I said here that an investigation was carried out, that an investigation judge, prosecutor, and the CSB, as well as the military security service were involved. The whole matter ended the way it did. I am not privy to the details of this process, and I cannot tell you anything more than I already did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could have P3852, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jankovic, you can see this is a security assessment for Prijedor municipality by the SMB of the Banja Luka CSB, dated the 23rd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And I would like to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In your testimony today, you were asked about Muslim and Croat villages which did not engage in fighting and which did not suffer any consequences or damage, and you identified a number of villages including Zecovi, Gornja and Donja Ravska, and Cela. Now, you can see in the third paragraph towards the top of the page, it says that dozens of villages have been almost completely destroyed and left uninhabited. And there is a list which includes Zecovi, and then it lists villages that have been partly destroyed, including Cela and Gornja and Donja Ravska. And it says this destruction saw the beginnings of the mass exodus of both Muslims and Croats. Now, you said these were villages that did not engage in fighting and which did not suffer any consequences or damage. That's not true, is it? These villages, Zecovi, Cela, and Gornja and Donja Ravska were either completely or partly destroyed; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: From what I can see, it's a report by the State Security Service. It was drafted by one Dusko Jelesic. I don't know who he received information from on this score. I know that in the area of what was formerly the municipality of Kozarac, there had been fighting and destruction. Let me just see. These are Croat villages. I don't think that there were such instances up there because a large portion of the Croat population was involved in the army -- was engaged in the Army of Republika Srpska. This may have been the case in part. However, I did not tour these villages and I cannot state for a fact if there were cases of suffering committed by individuals. I know that the area of Kozarac was destroyed in combat because there was war waged over there. It was impossible to tour these villages because there was a war on. It was impossible to find out exactly what was happening and what was not happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So is it correct, then, all those villages that you named in answer to Dr. Karadzic's questions, you didn't actually go to those villages to see what had happened there; is that right? I'm not talking about the ones in the document. I'm talking about the ones you identified in answer to Dr. Karadzic's questions.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't visit there, but I know from stories from when these events were happening that, for instance Gornja Puharska and Donja Puharska did not experience combat. Cerska, for instance, it did have, I can see here, but not Donja Puharska, except for the mosque which was destroyed. And if Jelisic thought that this was the case then it must have been the case. But there was no mass destruction in the villages that I mentioned. I didn't visit there but I know from stories that circulated that there was major destruction in the area of Kozarac, but I'm not familiar with these other places.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 22 and 23, the witness said: "For instance, Donja Puharska, Gornja Puharska," he didn't mention "Cerska," and that only a mosque was destroyed. And if Jelisic had but this in mind, the mosque, then that was it. But there was no other destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, probably we need to continue tomorrow. If you can finish in 15 minutes, we can --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try, Your Honours. I believe that I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, let's deal first with what was dealt with last. In this assessment made by the DB, it was said that there were departures of people. How did this come about? Did the authorities put pressure on the people to leave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- as far as I know in the area of Prijedor municipality --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Given that the witness said he never went to any of these places, I think a foundational question should be asked first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure that departures or evacuation of people were discussed, even. Did you raise that issue, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I didn't. It's stated in the document. But I didn't address that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At page 93, you were asked as a professional if you would let the perpetrators carry out sanitisation. Were all the members of these two platoons perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did perpetrators return to participate in sanitisation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And other members of the intervention platoon, so the entire platoon went up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is sanitisation something that is carried out before or after an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: After an on-site investigation. We had the representatives of the CSB Banja Luka there, the investigating judge, the prosecutor. I heard about it. I came into the whole process later, but I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Out of 1500 policemen who were mentioned to you at pages 93 and 94, how come only 50 or even less found their way on that payroll list of yours?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Because those were members of the active police force, and they were financed differently. There was a separate list drawn up for reserve policemen, which fell into three categories: The first category was retired policemen --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll have questions for you on that score. Where did those who were mobilised into the reserve police force receive their salary from? And they had their regular jobs.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it must have been the same companies where they were employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We should make a pause, really. The active policemen who were assigned to the wartime reserve police stations, where did they receive their salaries from and where were they administratively listed with?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: With the SJB Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please slow down and repeat what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, please repeat your question -- repeat your answer. Very, very slowly this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where were they administratively listed for the purposes of their salaries, their work records, those who were assigned to other stations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to active policemen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the public security station. That was their work-place. That was the organisation they worked for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 66 -- sorry, 5 -- P6678.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on page 1, Company 1 would be provided by some Prijedor police station, and then the 2nd Company would be provided by Prijedor police station 2. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was no Prijedor police station 2. Again, this is an error that was committed by the chief of the SJB who didn't know how the police worked. There was the reserve police station 1, reserve police station 2, reserve police station Brezicani, reserve police station Cikote, reserve police station Omarska, reserve police station Namovita [phoen], reserve police station Rakelici and Gomjenica, the reserve police station Tukovi, et cetera, and the reserve police station for traffic control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P6675.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, for that report you said that was a compilation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P6675. Can we look at page 6. Page 6 in Serbian. [In English] Next in Serbian. Next in English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, I'll read it out: "According to police precincts, the greatest number of offences were committed in the areas...," et cetera. What does this mean, the areas of departments?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when we were submitting a report, we were referring to the peacetime organisation in wartime circumstances because in Ljubija and Omarska we had police departments which were actually substations, and then elsewhere we had reserve police stations. So it was all based on the peacetime organisation or scheme because the wartime one wasn't referred to. I suppose that when reports were to be drawn up, they were to be drawn up on the basis of what was the organisation, like in peacetime, as defined in the rules governing the work of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- you were shown a document from the BH court stating that you disembarked at the site where the crime was committed and talked to Paras and Mrdja. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) He never said that I had any order issuing powers. He said what I said, that I was charged with material and technical equipment or, in other words, as we call it, the logistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will take care of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jankovic. No further questions. The Defence is grateful for the fact that you appeared as a witness.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Jankovic. On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You may be excused. The Chamber's thanks also go to Mr. Aleksic. Thank you very much. Before we adjourn, Mr. Robinson, coming back to the intercept issue, I presume that you'll be withdrawing the subpoena motion for KDZ145.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that's mentioned in one of the MFI conversion motions that we filed today, so you'll have a chance to rule on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are or you're not withdrawing that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue tomorrow. Next Witness Mudrinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be followed by Mr. Gruban.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of February, 2014, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
